issues.legal_issue: A court may give directions for the ordinary administration of a public trust under an existing management scheme without requiring a separate suit.
material_facts: A decree settling a management scheme appointed two joint managers and allowed either manager to apply to the court for directions when an occasion arose to carry out the scheme.
One manager applied for directions concerning the trust’s cattle and the cultivation of its lands; the managers were unable to agree.
The requested directions concerned the management and use of trust property.
issues.conclusion: The scheme authorized the court to give directions for ordinary administration on an application by a manager, without a separate suit.
issues.legal_principle: A suit under Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, section 92, to settle a scheme is analogous to an administration suit. A scheme may provide for its modification when necessary, and modifications for administration may be made on an application under the scheme without a separate section 92 suit. The Court followed Raje Anandrao v. Shamrao, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 930.

predicates.manager_applies_for_directions_under_exi: A manager of a trust applies to a court for directions under an existing management scheme.
predicates.scheme_authorizes_court_directions: The management scheme provides that a manager may seek court directions when needed to carry it out.
predicates.direction_concerns_ordinary_trust_admini: The requested direction concerns the ordinary administration of the trust.

issues.definition: When a manager seeks directions under a scheme that authorizes court directions and the matter concerns ordinary administration, the court may act under the scheme without a separate suit.

issues.legal_issue: The provision allowing court authorization of transactions involving trust property does not bar managers from ordinary administration of that property or prevent a scheme from providing for court directions on such management.
material_facts: A manager sought court directions to sell surplus cattle and lease cultivation rights in trust lands from year to year, relying on economy and practical utility.
The other manager objected, and the managers could not agree.
The court treated the requested measures as matters of ordinary administration of trust property.
issues.conclusion: The provision did not apply to these circumstances or require a separate suit; the court had jurisdiction under the scheme to give directions concerning the proposed management of trust property.
issues.legal_principle: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, section 92(1), clause (f), provides for court authorization to let, sell, mortgage, or exchange trust property in a suit under that section. It does not limit managers’ ordinary administration of trust property, including dealing with property for the trust’s benefit, and does not invalidate a scheme provision allowing managers to seek court directions. The Court relied on Raje Anandrao v. Shamrao, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 930, concerning directions and modifications for the purpose of administration.

predicates.manager_seeks_court_directions_on_trust_: A trust manager asks a court for directions concerning trust property.
predicates.proceeding_concerns_public_trust_managem: The proceeding concerns the management of a public trust.
predicates.proposed_transaction_is_ordinary_adminis: The proposed transaction is an ordinary measure for administering trust property for the trust’s benefit.

issues.definition: When a manager seeks directions in a public-trust management proceeding about a transaction that is ordinary administration, the transaction does not require a separate suit.
